target_customer: Product, design and engineering teams at companies that maintain a design system, from agencies to enterprises
problem: Design system documentation lived in stale PDFs, wikis and scattered files, so designers and developers did not share one source of truth.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription by team size and plan
product_category: Design system documentation and governance platform

founders.name: Jerome de Lafargue
founders.background_notes: Mobile app developer at Bloomberg where he met his co-founder; the founders committed fully to design systems in 2016 per the YC profile.

founders.name: Robin Tindale
founders.background_notes: Software engineer who met Jerome at Bloomberg.

technical_complexity.rationale: A documentation web app with integrations to design tools such as Sketch and Figma. Standard SaaS engineering for a two engineer founding team, with the integrations being the harder part.

defensibility.rationale: Once a team documents its system in the tool the content creates mild lock-in, but the early product was copyable and design tool vendors could add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Adobe became an investor in the 2021 Series A rather than a competitor. No acquisition found as of the sources read; the company remained independent.

market_need_then: Design systems were becoming common in product teams around 2016 to 2019 and teams needed a shared place to document components. By 2021 the company reported 1,300+ customers including Adobe and United Airlines.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, practitioner focused content marketing and case studies

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt launch of zeroheight 1.0 on 2015-11-13 and a steady stream of case studies and design community write ups; no merch or fan accounts found.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known in the design systems niche through case studies and community presence, but no press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: zeroheight rode the spread of design systems and Figma centered workflows, reached 1,300+ customers and a $10M Series A led by Tribe Capital in August 2021, and was still active in 2026 with about 55 staff. It has repositioned toward AI by offering an MCP server so coding agents can use a design system. No outcome search found a shutdown, acquisition or layoff, so it appears to be a steady independent growth company.
notes: Seedtable lists a 2019 seed of about 500K USD and a pre-seed of 150K USD, seen only on an aggregator, so unverified and not recorded as rounds. Aggregator totals conflict (about 10.4M to 20.65M). The YC page says founded 2015 while the batch was Summer 2019. No dated competitor sources from 2019 were found, so the list is empty. Outcome search for acquisition, layoffs or shutdown returned nothing relevant.
